newsitem.title: USA: Highlights of NYS Senate business tax cut plan.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of NYS Senate business tax cut plan.

text.p: The New York State Senate on Tuesday unveiled a new plan to slice business taxes by nearly $2.5 billion over five years that includes gradually eliminating state clothing sales taxes.
Highlights of the Senate program, unveiled by its Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno, follow.

--Freeze utility rates for 1997, begin phasing out the Gross Receipts Tax on Utilities, which produces $710 million of revenues. Enact Gov George Pataki's plan to give utilities targeted $60 million of tax cuts for economic development.
--Health Care Tax, phase out the Gross Receipts Tax on hospitals, nursing homes, health care clinics and home care providers. $550 million.

--Reform Estate and Gift Taxes, gradually raise the minimum filing level for state estate taxes to $600,000, while lowering estate tax rates. New York State then would adopt a "pick-up" of the Federal credit for state death taxes. The Senate also would repeal the gift tax. $300 million.

--Sales Tax on Clothing, exempt sales taxes in fiscal 1998 during two, one-week periods, one week in August and one week in January. The state sales tax on clothing that costs less than $500 would be phased out at one percent a year, with an option to gradually eliminate the local share of the sales tax. $550 million.

--Adoption Tax Credit, give state residents an income tax credit to offset some of the cost for adopting a child, defraying up to $5,000 of qualified expenses and up to $6,000 for adopting a child with special needs. $20 million.
--Child Care Tax Credit, give private sector companies tax credits for creating day care centers. $25 million.
--Small Business EDZ Employment Incentive Credit, give employment incentive credits to small businesses. $5 million.

--Extension of Investment Tax Credit Carry-forward, extend to 15 years from 10 years the period that unused credits can be carried forward, bringing the state in line with the federal government. $20 million.
--Eliminate Mutual Fund Threshold Requirement that requires portfolios to consist of at least 50 percent of federal obligations to be exempt from state income tax. $19 million.

--Insurance Tax Reforms--Repeal Article 15 that makes auto insurers pre-pay the sales tax on damage awards. New York life insurance companies would gain from a premiums tax cap change, making them more competitive with other states.
--Repeal Beverage Container Tax and Excise Tax on Beer, repealing the remainder of these taxes. $45 million.
--Eliminate the Petroleum Busines Tax on Railroads. $5 million.
--Repeal Indexing the Petroleum Business Tax, which is passed along to consumers of various fuel. This would not impact funds dedicated for highways, bridges and mass transit. $40 million.
--Disability Employment Credit, provide a tax credit to employers who hire disabled employees.
